output.summary: The run is VALID with COMPLETE analysis coverage, and the deterministic policy verdict is FAIL: policy check rule_id "latency" observed response_time_p95_ms = 550 ms with operator lte against threshold 200 ms, so the window verdict is FAIL (business_verdict FAIL, resource_verdict NO_POLICY). Error counts are 0 across 60000 overall samples and 28919 window samples, so this is a latency-based failure, not an error-based one. Generated load shows target_rate constant at 100 requests/s while achieved request_starts averaged ~60.25 requests/s (median 40, min 30, max 100, slope per second ~-0.186) and active_threads varied between 5 and 20 (mean ~14.37). A correlation pair (association-09) reports raw rho ~0.998274 between active_threads and response_time_p95_ms at best_lag_ms -1000, but it is status CANDIDATE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, the headline MBB Holm p-value is UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED), and clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; therefore no lead/lag or causal interpretation is supported. Advice: preserve the FAIL verdict, verify clock alignment before any temporal analysis, obtain a statistically supported correlation result, drill into the ~550 ms latency tail (p50=50 ms while p95=p99=max=550 ms), and investigate why the generator did not sustain the constant 100 rps target.
